Findings for review

Each goes to its owner; the tree changes only after a person reviews it

▲
2 sets the drawn tree does not predict
{BE-1.13}, {BE-1.17}: the SoC reads the same stuck cruise frame as the envelope, so on a cancel it stays engaged and keeps commanding without a SoC fault (DFI-10). The cut-set table already calls them single points; the drawn tree keeps BE-1.15 as a second event.
▲
5 tree sets the model does not reach
{BE-1.18}, {BE-1.12, BE-1.15}, {BE-1.13, BE-1.15}, {BE-1.15, BE-1.16} and others. BE-1.12: one corrupted frame opens the TSR-301 engagement window, and the next genuine 0x1D2 (cruise inactive) revokes within one step; a replay that holds cruise active acts as BE-1.13. BE-1.16: a brake press also drops PCM cruise, so the envelope revokes on 0x1D2 (TSR-301) and the SoC disengages on it; a stuck brake frame matters only with a stuck cruise frame too. BE-1.18: a debug build has no envelope, but the SoC still gates its own command on its engagement, so the model needs a SoC fault too; the tree takes the missing envelope as the failure (configuration single point).
✕
3 stale-torque single points remain
A stale model input (BE-1.19), masked diagnostics (BE-1.20) and a replayed command buffer (BE-1.21) hold torque past the FTTI: the heartbeat and frame-arrival checks do not see a stale value in frames that keep arriving (TSR-409 open). TSR-602 drops a stale model input only at 0.52 s, just over the 0.5 s FTTI.
▲
Plant case F-03: nothing reacts
With the command frozen and the heartbeat alive, the panda does not react. The driver notices the drift at 1.47 s and steers at 2.96 s, after the car crosses the lane line at 2.09 s.
